It started with nothing more than a lazy afternoon in Castorice’s dorm lounge, warm light filtering through the curtains, the smell of instant ramen, and the distinct sound of Cipher’s amused cackling as she scrolled through their shared group chat.

Mydei, in contrast, sat upright at the small coffee table with a sleek kitchenware catalog in his lap, brows slightly furrowed in concentration as he traced his finger along the fine print beside a high-end chef’s knife. His eyes glinted in admiration. A familiar look that Cipher and Castorice had been quietly observing for weeks.

Cipher suddenly let out a sharp, pleased sound. “Oh, guess who’s hosting a pool party next weekend?”

Mydei didn’t look up. “Unless it's Phainon, I don’t care.”

Cipher grinned like the cat that caught the canary. “It is Phainon.”

That got Mydei’s attention. His gaze flicked up, but only briefly. “So?”

“So,” Castorice cut in, flipping herself upright, “this is your chance.”

“My chance for what?” Mydei asked warily, closing his catalog a little too fast. Cipher and Castorice exchanged looks.

“To confess your undying love,” Cipher said sweetly.

“To seduce the man of your dreams,” Castorice added with a dramatic flutter of her lashes.

Mydei gave them both a look. “I don’t have a crush on Phainon.”

“Mhm,” Cipher said with a smirk. “Is that why you go quiet every time he walks into a room?”

“And practically melt when he so much as nods at you?” Castorice added, grinning wickedly.

“Must be a coincidence that your shirt magically gets tighter when he’s around,” Cipher teased.

“Or shorter,” Castorice added.

“I wear the same shirt every day.”

“Exactly,” they said in unison.

Mydei groaned and pinched the bridge of his nose. “You’re both insufferable.”

“And you’re in love.” Cipher sang.

“Hopelessly in love.” Castorice echoed, clasping her hands together in mock-sincerity.

Cipher sat up, eyes gleaming. “Which is why we have a proposition.”

“No.”

“You haven’t even heard it yet!” Castorice said, nearly bouncing on the couch.

“I already know it’s ridiculous.” Mydei sighed.

“Let us dream, Mydei,” Cipher sighed dramatically. “So here it is: you show up to Phainon’s pool party wearing the most revealing women’s swimsuit you can find.”

“I’m sure you’d look great too!” Castorice said excitedly, holding up her fingers like she was envisioning the cut.

“If you get a reaction out of him, like, any crack in that puppy’s face—” Cipher continued.

“Eyebrows raised. A double-take. The slightest jaw drop. Anything,” Castorice finished.

“Then we’ll buy you every single thing on your little wish list. Even that overpriced mixer you pretended not to want last week.”

“And the kitchen knife,” Mydei said flatly.

Cipher groaned. “Why is it always the kitchen knife?”

“Because I need it,” Mydei snapped.

“Fine, princess, the knife too,” Cipher said, throwing her hands up. “But,” she added, grinning, “if you don’t get a reaction, we post the pictures of you in the swimsuit to our group chat, and Phainon will be haunted by them forever.”

Mydei’s eye twitched. “That wasn’t part of the original deal.”

“It is now,” Cipher said sweetly.

“This is such a dumb idea,” he muttered.

“Is it?” Castorice said, leaning in. “Or is it actually the perfect plan to get you and your dream boy in the same pool, at the same time, with nothing but three inches of fabric and some tension so thick we could cut it with one of those knives you keep crying over?”

Cipher clapped once. “So cute.”

“Adorable even.” Castorice added.

“You two are insane.” Mydei replied.

“But he's your type,” Cipher whispered. “All whimsy and puppy-like and probably packing.”

Mydei turned bright red. “Cipher—!”

“Oh no, don’t act shocked,” Castorice snorted. “You’ve thought about it.”

“Multiple times,” Cipher chimed.

“I have not.”

Both girls stared at him.

He folded instantly. “Okay. Maybe once.”

“Aha!” they said together.

Mydei groaned again, burying his face in his hands. But when he looked up, there was something different in his eyes. A twitch of curiosity. Maybe a little mischief.
“So,” he said slowly, “if I do this… you’re really buying me everything?”

“Every. Single. Thing.” Cipher swore. “You show skin, we show money.”

Mydei leaned back in his chair, arms crossed, eyes narrowed in thought. Then, slowly, a smirk tugged at the corner of his mouth.

“Alright,” he said. “I’ll do it. But I’m choosing the swimsuit.”

“Oh, please do,” Castorice purred. “At least you have good fashion taste unlike someone else…”

“Don’t diss his little boyfriend like that, you’ll hurt our dear Mydeimos’ feelings.” Cipher said, sarcastically.

“Phainon won’t survive this,” Castorice muttered gleefully.

And Mydei?
He was already imagining the look in Phainon’s eyes when he would reveal what he was truly wearing, smiling to himself.

They were going to regret this.

Mydei now found himself seated cross-legged on Castorice’s bed, a laptop in front of him, Cipher and Castorice flanking him on either side like a pair of gremlins hungry for chaos.

“Alright,” Cipher said, already cracking her knuckles. “Let’s find you the sluttiest swimsuit on the Internet.”

“Yeah,” Castorice added, her eyes gleaming with excitement. “But like, also elegant if you get me.”

“This is ridiculous,” Mydei muttered, though he made no move to close the laptop.

“Shut up, you’re enjoying this,” Cipher said, clicking through the first site and immediately filtering for Women’s Swimwear > Bikinis > Minimal coverage.

“Oh,” Castorice gasped, leaning in. “Look at this one—lace and mesh. It’s like lingerie’s trashy cousin.”

“Too try-hard,” Cipher said, waving it off. “We need something that’ll look effortless. Like he just woke up, threw it on, and still managed to make Phainon question everything about his life.”

They spent the next half hour laughing, debating, and bookmarking increasingly criminal options. Some were too complicated: straps wrapped around the torso like a spiderweb. Others too loud: bright pink ruffles or glitter that would flake off into the pool. But then, just as Mydei was about to suggest giving up for the night, Castorice let out a sharp gasp.
“Oh. Oh my god. Click that one.”

Cipher did, and then all three of them went quiet.

The image on the screen was unapologetic. A dark red two-piece bikini.

Perfect.

The top was made of two tiny triangles that barely qualified as fabric, held together by thin string that tied at the neck and back. The bottom was a thong cut high on the hips, the front narrow, the back virtually nonexistent. Shiny, sleek, and criminally minimal.

“This is basically just two napkins and a shoestring,” Mydei said flatly.

“Exactly,” Cipher whispered, eyes wide with reverence.

“It’s perfect,” Castorice added, already zooming in on the model photos. “It’ll show off your hips, your waist, your everything. He’s going to implode.”

“Do you want to make Phainon malfunction or not?” Cipher asked.

Mydei stared at the screen for a long moment. Objectively, it was absurd. Practically a dare in swimsuit form. But the thought of slipping into that thing and catching Phainon’s eyes just once? The idea burned hotter than he wanted to admit.

“Add to cart,” he said.

Castorice screamed.

Cipher did a victory roll across the bed.

As the order confirmation hit the screen, Mydei leaned back, arms crossed, lips curling into a sly, dangerous smile.

What will Phainon do when he sees me in this?

He didn’t say it out loud, but the question was already burning in his mind.

And whatever the answer was, he was ready for it.

Morning passed in a blur, and by the time the sun began to dip into late afternoon—just golden enough to promise a perfect poolside glow—he found himself standing alone in his room, staring at the tiny red bikini laid out on his bed like it was taunting him.

“I can’t wear this,” he muttered under his breath, pressing his fingers to his temples. “There’s no way. I’ll walk in, and Phainon will—”

A message from Cipher lit up his phone.
Tell me you’re already wearing it. We’re leaving in 15 minutes.

He adjusted the strings slightly, let out one final breath, and grabbed a mesh cover-up that didn’t do much but gave him the illusion of dignity.

He hesitated, then accepted.

Her voice came through immediately, sharp and demanding:

“I’m wearing it,” Mydei said flatly, eyes still locked on his mirror image.

A pause.

“Prove it.”

One quick snap—nothing too revealing (which was ironic, considering the swimsuit)—but enough to show the deep plunge of the red triangles, the impossibly high straps hugging his hips, yet he added a small cat sticker covering the small bit of his dick that wasn’t cooperating with him by staying in the damn fabric.

“Oh my fucking god?”

He winced, pulling the phone slightly away from his ear.

“Mydei you look fucking insane!?”

“You told me to wear something that would make him react,” Mydei said dryly.

“React?! He’s going to combust! He’s going to forget his own name. You’re going to short-circuit his brain, Mydei. Do you know what this is?!”

“You’re overreacting.”

“I am not.” Cipher was breathless now.

Mydei rubbed his temple, though a small smile tugged at the corners of his mouth. “Should I change?”

“If you change, I will fight you. Do not rob the world—do not rob Phainon—of this moment.”

He laughed under his breath.

“I’m serious,” Cipher went on, manic. “He’s gonna see you walk in like that and just—die. Right there. Just kneel over. You win. Instantly. And I will take a photo of that expression to frame above my bed.”

“Tell Castorice to stop doubting me,” Mydei said, putting back his shirt on.

“She’s already on the floor screaming into a pillow. You’ve done God’s work, Mydeimos.”

Another pause.

“Hey, Mydei?”

“Yeah?”

“I mean it when I say that you’re gonna kill him.”

He smirked at his reflection—half-naked, barely covered, tattoos on full display, and a quiet, dangerous confidence settling in behind his eyes.

“I know.”

And with that, he hung up.

By the time Mydei arrived at Phainon’s pool party, the sun was casting long golden streaks over the water, the air warm and heady with the scent of sunscreen, citrus cocktails, and grilled meat.

Mydei stood just outside the gate, nerves coiled tight in his chest like a spring. Despite Cipher’s and Castorice’s enthusiastic screeching over their group chat all morning, he had made a last-minute decision: he threw on a plain black shirt. He rang the doorbell.

It opened less than five seconds later.

At Mydei’s bare thighs.
At the clean, golden lines of muscle.

Barely concealed smiles. Raised brows.

Silence.

Back to the pool. Back to the water.

Still there. Still Mydei.

Hyacine leaned over the pool edge, whispering like she was watching a nature documentary. “Look at him. Poor thing’s short-circuiting.”

Mydei, finally easing back into himself, now sitting like any normal person would—hips shifting just enough to make the thong straps tighten around his waist.
